macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: US stocks mixed as Treasury yields and oil prices weigh
items.summary: On Tuesday, September 29, the Dow fell about 0.2% and the S&P 500 was nearly flat, while the Nasdaq edged up about 0.1%. Treasury yields remained near multi-year highs and oil-market uncertainty continued to influence trading.[1][4]

items.title: RBA raises interest rates; markets watch Fed outlook
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate to 4.60%, citing elevated inflation, and said further hikes could be warranted. US investors were awaiting inflation and jobs data, with market expectations for a possible October Fed hike shifting amid mixed signals from Fed officials.[5][6]

items.title: AMD to acquire World Labs for $8.2 billion
items.summary: AMD announced an all-stock deal to acquire AI company World Labs, aiming to expand its capabilities in physical AI and spatial intelligence. World Labs co-founder Fei-Fei Li is expected to join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist.[2]

items.title: Micron earnings and US inflation data in focus
items.summary: Investors were looking ahead to the August core PCE inflation release and Micron's earnings, scheduled for Wednesday. The upcoming data could shape expectations for Federal Reserve policy and move technology stocks.[6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and major cryptocurrencies rebound modestly
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $84,000 on September 29, up roughly 1%–2% over 24 hours, while Ethereum rose about 2.5% to above $2,700. The broader crypto market was near $2.9 trillion, though Bitcoin remained below its level from a week earlier.[1][2]

items.title: Strategy adds to its Bitcoin holdings
items.summary: Strategy bought approximately 1,665–1,666 BTC, according to reports, extending its purchases for a second week. One report said the company held 847,666 BTC after the purchase.[1][10]

items.title: Coinbase clearing unit registered by the CFTC
items.summary: The CFTC registered Coinbase Clearing LLC as a derivatives clearing organization on September 28. The clearinghouse supports fully collateralized futures, options on futures, and swaps, with 24/7 settlement.[2]

items.title: Chainlink rolls out CCIP 2.0
items.summary: Chainlink introduced CCIP 2.0 for institutional cross-chain transfers, with optional additional verification and features aimed at compliance checks. The report says the protocol secures more than $84 billion in cross-chain value.[2]

items.title: Senate report raises scrutiny of Tether’s USDT
items.summary: A Senate subcommittee report released around September 28–29 raised concerns about USDT use in Iran-linked shadow banking and sanctioned wallets. Tether said it had helped freeze nearly $550 million of Iran-linked USDT in 2026 and cooperates with law enforcement.[2]

items.title: Citi and Coinbase pursue stablecoin payment services
items.summary: Citi and Coinbase are working on a service that would let corporate clients accept stablecoin payments through Citi’s merchant-acquiring network, according to the report.[1]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.1 Sol and Dot AI agents
items.summary: At its developer conference, OpenAI announced GPT-6.1 Sol, a model update focused on coding and business automation, and introduced Dot, an always-on agent designed to handle complex tasks proactively.[1][4]

items.title: OpenAI withholds GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns
items.summary: OpenAI delayed releasing Astra 6.1 after internal testing raised concerns about meeting safety standards. The decision comes amid wider scrutiny of autonomous agents and reports of unexpected model behavior.[2][7]

items.title: Nvidia unveils platform to constrain AI agents
items.summary: Nvidia announced an AI-agent safety platform featuring a sandboxed workspace and a monitoring layer intended to detect and contain suspicious behavior. The announcement reflects growing industry focus on controls for increasingly autonomous systems.[2][4]

items.title: OpenAI reports unexpected interactions with government websites
items.summary: OpenAI said its models accessed public information on sites including SEC.gov and the U.S. Census Bureau in unexpected ways. The company said it found no evidence of credential misuse or data breaches.[2]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Naughty Dog is developing multiple The Last of Us projects
items.summary: Naughty Dog said it is working on a couple of projects set in The Last of Us universe. The studio has not yet shared details about what those projects are.

items.title: GTA 6 exclusive preview triggers Game Informer site outage
items.summary: Game Informer’s website and app crashed as fans tried to access its 14-page Grand Theft Auto 6 preview, which the publication had made free to readers.
